CNC-02, on a separate branch, maintains stable pressure (E5), ruling out a general supply issue. The manual (E2) confirms that a leak or pump issue would cause pressure to fall continuously, even during idle periods, and that this would not recover without repair. The inspection results (E6) show no rejects from CNC-05, but the manual notes that a leak may not yet have caused failures, especially if the pressure drop is recent. H2 (supply restriction) is less likely because CNC-02’s pressure remains stable, and a branch restriction would not explain the gradual decline while idle.
result.discriminating_check: get_readings for CNC-05 hydraulic_pressure from tick 1100 to 1290 with a focus on idle periods (e.g., ticks 1220–1290, when CNC-05 was idle) to confirm whether pressure continued to fall without recovery, or if there were brief spikes above the setpoint (which would suggest a leak rather than a supply restriction).

objections.text: No inspection rejects from CNC-05 are shown (E6), so the expected symptom of workpiece shifting due to low clamping pressure is unconfirmed.
H2 (supply restriction) cannot be ruled out entirely without direct evidence of a branch-specific issue, though CNC-02’s stable pressure weakens it.

anomaly: alarm on CNC-02: hydraulic_pressure 54.46 bar below 55.00
conclusion: CNC-02 has an intermittent hydraulic restriction (sticking valve or partially clogged filter) causing transient pressure drops below the 55 bar setpoint — a physical fault localized to CNC-02, not a one-off sensor glitch and not normal load draw. Hydraulic pressure fell to 54.46 bar at tick 1041 (the alarm) and a second sub-55 dip, 54.90 bar, recurred at tick 1052, with full recovery between dips and pressure back to 59.18 bar at tick 1050. Load was already high and steady (~48 bar) from tick 1035 with no spike at 1041, vibration stayed normal, inspections passed, and sibling hydraulic machine CNC-05 stayed stable around 66-71 bar with no dips, so CNC-01, CNC-03, CNC-04, CNC-06 and CNC-05 show no matching fault.
unresolved_questions: Distinguish H2 (intermittent physical restriction) from H1 (repeated transducer noise): two sub-55 dips are observed but not conclusively differentiated.
CNC-07 also has hydraulics but its pressure was never checked; it has no symptom or alarm, so it is untested rather than cleared.
Does the CNC-02 pressure dip at tick 1041 occur without any corresponding load increase (favoring a physical intermittent restriction over normal load draw)?
Did CNC-02 pressure recover to 59.18 bar at tick 1050 while load remained high (~47 bar), which would contradict a pure load-draw explanation and favor a transient or sensor cause?
next_check: Record CNC-02 hydraulic_pressure and load over the next ~30 ticks to confirm recurrence and that dips occur without load changes before a human authorizes repair_hydraulics.
action_rationale: Confidence (0.80) is below the 0.90 intervene threshold, so no repair is auto-authorized. CNC-02 is running but repeatedly dips below 55 bar (ticks 1041 and 1052) with full recovery and no load correlation, risking a sustained fault or quality escape. Escalate to a human to confirm the restriction (valve/filter) and authorize repair_hydraulics (stops CNC-02 about 40 ticks, replaces seals) or further diagnostics; afterwards expect pressure to remain at or above 55 bar with no recurrent dips under comparable load.
